name: @stonedogcode/featuremap
description: The feature-map schema: what a repository declares about its own features and the code paths that implement them, validated so a coverage gate can refuse a malformed map as a different verdict from an uncovered file.
author: StoneDogCode L.L.C.
//exports: `.` is the library. `./schema` is the raw JSON Schema, exported as a file so a consumer in another language -- the gate may end up a composite action running anything -- can read it without a JavaScript import.
//files: src/ ships as TypeScript SOURCE, matching @stonedogcode/tests. __tests__ is excluded because those import jest globals and a consumer parsing src/** would drag them in.

scripts.//build:action: Bundle src/action into dist/index.js, the single file GitHub runs. Committed, because a JavaScript action has no install step.
scripts.//check:bundle: Rebuild and refuse a diff. dist/index.js is what CI executes in every consuming repo, so a stale bundle runs the OLD logic and reports success.
scripts.//check:action: Is action.yml a manifest GitHub will LOAD? Nothing else checks it -- actionlint lints workflows, check:bundle compares the bundle, and the e2e runs dist/index.js directly. Both defects it catches shipped as v1.0.0 and failed in the consuming repo.
scripts.//test: Jest runs as ESM, which needs the VM modules flag.
scripts.//test:integration: Validates the REAL maps in this fleet, not fixtures. That is the seam: a schema that only ever sees its own examples has not been shown to accept the corpus it was written for.
scripts.//gate: Everything that must pass before a publish. Named so publish-package.sh has one thing to call and cannot drift from what CI runs.
scripts.gate: npm run type-check && npm run lint && npm run test && npm run test:integration
scripts.//verify:package: Pack, install the tarball into a temp directory as a consumer, typecheck through the PUBLISHED exports map and then RUN the validator in BOTH directions. `files`, `exports` and the tarball contents are invisible to a test suite operating on source files in this repo, and they are exactly what breaks at publish time -- after review, when the version is already burned. Both directions because a truncated schema file accepts every document, so checking only that valid maps pass would prove nothing.
scripts.//publish:stonedog-featuremap: Run from a terminal, INTERACTIVELY -- npm prompts for the 2FA one-time password and the login flow needs a browser, so an agent cannot complete it. You need not log in first: it starts `npm login` itself if needed. It refuses a checkout that is detached, dirty, not on main, or behind origin/main; refuses a version the registry already has; refuses an account that is not an owner of an existing package (which would fail as a misleading 404); runs the gate and verify:package; then proves the result by installing from the registry and resolving the ./schema export, because a data file's absence is invisible until someone reads it.
scripts.//validate: The CLI the gate will call. Exits 0 valid, 1 invalid, 2 unreadable -- three states, because 'could not open the file' is not 'the file is wrong'.
